statements.title: the zero-count criterion: χ_λ(g_{p/q}) ≠ 0 iff N_q(λ+ρ) = N_q(ρ), at every rational point of the ρ-line
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Theorem 3.1 from the product (2): if F_ρ·Q = F_ℓ, then Q(ζ) ≠ 0 at a primitive q-th root iff N_q(ℓ) = N_q(ρ), and N_q(ρ) ≤ N_q(ℓ); eval_quot gives the exact value when the counts agree. Not formalized: that ζ^{−(λ,ρ)}Q(ζ) is the character (formula (2), Weyl), certified exactly in certificar_exacto.py (C1); and that F_ρ divides F_ℓ, taken as hypothesis.; added to the Lean repository after publication (09-nov-2026): The product (2) is a polynomial: F_ρ divides F_ℓ for every ℓ of length m with positive pairings (ρ minimizes N_d for every d), so Theorems 3.1, 7.1 and 8.3 hold in Lean without the quotient hypothesis. Only the identification of ζ^{−(λ,ρ)}Q(ζ) with the character (formula (2), Weyl) is outside Lean.

statements.title: the alphabet of a_P^k is d·μ_q less two letters: two copies of 1 (d even), or 1 and −1 (d odd)
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (23-oct-2026): Covers Proposition 4.1 in full, as multisets over an arbitrary field with a primitive (2m+2)-th root of unity.

statements.title: every character is an integer at g_{1/q} exactly for q | 2m, q | 2m+1, q | 2m+2, or q = 6 with m ≡ 1 (mod 3)
statements.formal_part: the classification of the Galois-stable segments, by another route (Amiot’s lemma, not the Dirichlet kernels of the proof): for n ≥ 3 and a unit a ≢ ±1, {±1, …, ±m} mod n is stable under a iff n divides 2m, 2m+1 or 2m+2; not the link with integrality, nor q ∈ {3, 4, 6}; added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Theorem 5.1 at the level of the spectrum, for every q ≥ 2 (q = 3, 4, 6 included): the spectrum {±1, …, ±m} is Galois-stable iff the divisibility condition holds, and the elementary symmetric functions of the spectrum are integers iff it is Galois-stable. Not formalized: that every character of Sp(2m) is an integer iff those symmetric functions are (the representation ring), certified exactly in certificar_exacto.py (C2).

statements.title: type C: χ_λ(a_P^k) ≠ 0 iff no folded class modulo q holds more than d of the ℓ_i (⌊d/2⌋ on a fixed class)
statements.formal_part: the counting half over ZMod q: N_q(x) ≥ N_q(ρ), with equality iff the capacities hold (the link to the character is Theorem 3.1, not formalized)

statements.title: the one unit of slack: m = dq/2 − 1 rows against a total capacity dq/2 (d even) or dq/2 − 1 (d odd)
statements.formal_part: in the unfolded form over ZMod q: the deficits d − o_x(g) add up to 2, and under the capacities exactly one folded class falls one short (d even) or the occupancies are saturated (d odd)

statements.title: the value at every power, sign included: χ_λ(a_P^k) = (−1)^{E_{p,q}(λ)} Z_q(λ+ρ)/Z_q(ρ) on the survivors, 0 elsewhere
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (09-nov-2026): Theorem 7.1 in full, as stated in the note (no adjustment of E): the exact value with its sign at every power, from formula (2), with the divisibility F_ρ | F_ℓ as a hypothesis as in Theorem 3.1.

statements.title: at k = 2, the absolute value is a product of one factor per folded class
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Theorem 8.1 in the form by pairings: at k = 2 every divisible pairing of ρ equals q, so ‖Q(ζ)‖ = ∏_{q∣(ℓ,α)} (ℓ,α)/q. The regrouping into one factor D_c per folded class is notation over this product and is not stated separately; formula (2) and the divisibility as in Theorem 3.1.

statements.title: the non-vanishing part of the C_{q−1} Weyl product over μ_q less one point does not depend on the point
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Proposition 8.2 in full, in the ordered form M_s² = V_s·C_s·D_s: the punctured Vandermonde is q^{q−2} and C_s·D_s = q^{q−2}·D, so the product does not depend on the removed point.

statements.title: the absolute value at any power is the ratio of the vanishing root values, |χ| = Z_q(ℓ)/Z_q(ρ)
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Theorem 8.3: at the powers of a_P (dq = 2m + 2), ‖Q(ζ)‖ = ∏_{q∣(ℓ,α)}(ℓ,α) / ∏_{q∣(ρ,α)}(ρ,α), for any ℓ with positive pairings and N_q(ℓ) = N_q(ρ); with formula (2) and the divisibility as in Theorem 3.1.

statements.title: the surviving factors of the limit have modulus one
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Lemma 8.4 in full: the non-vanishing factors of ℓ and of ρ have the same modulus at a primitive q-th root, q | 2m + 2, through the residue lemma (ResidueCapacity.prop_res_cap).

statements.title: the residue lemma: ℛ_x = (P_x(X)² + P_x(X²))/2 − m in ℤ[X]/(X^q − 1), and ℛ_{λ+ρ} = ℛ_ρ under the capacities
statements.formal_part: the identity in the form 2ℛ_x + 2m = P_x² + P_x(X²) over a finite abelian group, and ℛ_x = ℛ_ρ under the capacities over ZMod q

statements.title: the difference of the two residue histograms is the histogram of another root system, C_r or D_r
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (09-nov-2026): Proposition 9.2 in full, in both regimes (type C_r for v ≤ a, type D_r for v > a), with S₀ identified as ρ_H. S is given as a list of representatives in arbitrary order (the note orders it decreasingly; the histograms do not see the order).

statements.title: the modulus factors as κ ∈ {1, 2} times dimensions of GL_n, Sp_2n and SO_2n+1 representations, one per folded class
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (09-nov-2026): Theorem 10.1 for odd d (κ = 1), in modulus: one dimension per folded class (GL on the non-fixed classes, Sp on the class 0, SO on the class q/2). The occupancies of the classes (s, s, 2s+1) are hypotheses, not yet derived from the capacities; the case of even d (κ ∈ {1, 2}) is not formalized.; added to the Lean repository after publication (09-nov-2026): Theorem 10.1 in both parities, with κ ∈ {1, 2} and the occupancies derived from N_q(ℓ) = N_q(ρ). The partitions ν^{(c)} and the oriented rows are taken as given data with their defining equations (that ν is a partition is not proved), and the statement is for lists ℓ of length m (the step from a dominant λ to ℓ = λ + ρ is not stated).

statements.title: a closed count of the surviving residues modulo q, for every q, in type C
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Theorem 11.1 in full, for every q (no q | 2m + 2): N_q as the convex cost of the folded occupancies, the minimal profiles in both regimes, and the closed count #{x ∈ (ℤ/q)^m : N_q(x) = N_q(ρ)}, stated in ℕ with the denominators cleared.

statements.title: in G_2 the vanishing at q = 3 and q = 2 is a congruence on (a, b)
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (23-oct-2026): The Lean covers the arithmetic of the G₂ corollary (the two congruences on N_q versus r_q); the link to the vanishing of the character is the paper criterion and is not formalized.

statements.title: read through coroots, R_P(q) contains the R(q) of the dual group, with equality when gcd(q, r) = 1
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (08-nov-2026): Observation 13.1 over any crystallographic root pairing with a base: the coroot coefficients in the dual base, ht_P(α) = ((α,α)/2)·ht(α^∨) = (ρ,α), and the three clauses. Taken as hypotheses: the two root lengths ((α,α)/2 ∈ {1, r}) and a ρ with ⟨ρ, α_i^∨⟩ = 1.
